reference_image.description: Path to the reference image reused across segments, or null.

description.description: Canonical identity line, copied verbatim into every segment prompt.

style_lock.description: One line locking the visual style for the whole video.

world_rules.description: Immutable rules of the world (lighting direction, physics, no-new-characters, etc.).

action.description: Primary action, concrete verbs, in order.

angle.description: e.g. low angle, dutch angle, high angle, POV

size.description: e.g. close-up, medium, full body, extreme wide

move.description: e.g. push-in, orbit, whip pan, dolly, tilt

beats.description: The internal timed beats/locations chained INSIDE this single segment prompt via hard/whip cuts. A beat is a short event (e.g. a 0.5–1s location change in a hyper-lapse). This is the list that gets compressed into ONE segment prompt as internal [Shot N] markers — one prompt per segment, never one prompt per beat. Omit or leave empty for a segment that is a single continuous shot with no internal cuts.

location_or_event.description: The location/setting of this beat, or the event if not a location change.

action.description: What the subject does in this beat (expression + gesture).

outfit.description: The distinctive outfit worn in this beat.

transition_in.description: The first beat/composition of this segment that the cut bridges — ideally a framing different from the previous segment's ending.

transition_out.description: The last beat/composition of this segment that the cut bridges — the framing the next segment should open on a different angle/size than.

cut.description: The cinematic edit that connects this segment to the previous one. Replaces last-frame conditioning: segments are joined by intentional cuts (j-cut, l-cut, straight-cut, match-cut, whip-pan, action-cut, cutaway) on CONTRASTING compositions, never by feeding one clip's final frame into the next.

type.description: The edit type used to enter this segment.

description.description: How the cut is executed and what carries the eye across it.

audio_overlap_seconds.description: For j-cut/l-cut: how many seconds of audio cross the cut (audio from the next segment for j-cut, from the previous for l-cut). null for a straight-cut.

ends_on.description: Framing/angle of this segment's final beat (e.g. medium close-up, low angle).

opens_on.description: Contrasting framing/angle the NEXT segment must open on, so the cut reads as an intentional edit, not a stuttered first-frame match.

sound_cue.description: Designed sound/music reference for H3 to generate (it produces music and foley with the video). Can be used to set up a j-cut/l-cut by introducing the next segment's audio early.

reference_image.description: Reference image file reused for this segment (from references), or null.

ref2va.description: The self-contained full-reference (ref2va) rewrite for this segment, ready to paste into an image-to-video / text-to-video job. Labels are scoped to this segment.

subject_definitions.description: One line per reference label used in this segment (<Subject N> / <Picture N> / <Video N> / <Audio N>), with the reference-image source cited inside <Subject N> definitions when the look is locked from a sheet.

summary.description: One paragraph beginning with a square-bracketed task-type prefix (e.g. [reference generation + keyframe completion]).

retention_analysis.description: One line per label with a fixed relationship marker: fully_preserved / partially_preserved / attribute_transfer / weak_reference.

detailed_description.description: Style opening + shot-by-shot (per-beat) playback order with reference labels, (Sx) speaker IDs, and <d>[Language] dialogue. One prompt per segment: internal beats are [Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm markers relative to the segment start. Scaled to the ~12-15s clip, not the number of beats; not the full 350-500 word whole-video range.

overall_soundscape.description: Ambience and physical sounds H3 generates: fully stated (what is heard, texture, level, entry/exit). Complete generation instructions, not a terse post-prod reference.

non_diegetic_music.description: Audience-only background score H3 generates: instrumentation, tempo, dynamics; N/A only if deliberately silent.

references.description: Pre-production reference sheets generated with an image model, then consumed by H3 image-to-video to lock identity/continuity.

generation_prompt.description: Prompt to generate the turnaround/reference sheet with an image model

key_frame_file.description: Filename of the chosen key frame fed to H3

inventory.description: Pre-determined counts of what must be locked, determined before generating any sheet (see the skill's Step 2). character_sheets, environment_sheets, and prop_sheets each must contain at least this many entries.

continuity_manifest.description: Maps each subject to its reference file and the segments that reuse it, so the generator never guesses which image to feed.

subject.description: e.g. protagonist, ink sword, moonlit ink landscape

weight.description: e.g. high, medium, low reference strength
